newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees more L/American orders.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees more L/American orders.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a number of new orders on Thursday with Latin America again featuring among popular origins, shipbrokers said.
London-based CR Sugar was open for 9/10,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Rio de Janeiro to west Africa for prompt dates.
CSR quoted for 16,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to the Indonesian port of Cigading, again for prompt.
Shipbrokers said Louis Dreyfus was in the market for 18,700 tonnes in bulk from the Philippines to U.S. west coast for prompt/seven days notice.

Genoc amended the dates on its recent 14,000-tonne bulk Cuba order to Casablanca, Portugal, Mediterranean, Adriatic and Black Sea options to 14/21 March. Cargill's order for 8,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to Japan was still open and the charterer issued a new bulk order on the same run for 18,000 tonnes with South Korea option for the beginning of March.

The only firm business reported came from Booker, which fixed 7,500/10,000 tonnes from Georgetown to UK/Nantes for February 21/March 3. In other news, Iraq issued a tender for February 25 to buy 120,000 tonnes of white sugar and the results are still awaited in Iran's recent tender for 14,000 tonnes of whites and 30,000 tonnes of raws, both cargoes for April shipment.
